channel.description: Daily news scored for its impact on Capital goods & infra in Indian markets. Today: tailwind (+2.4).

item.title: [+1] Scotland raises Scotch whisky tariff dispute with India as trade deal faces first major test
item.description:
Signal: trade deal or tariff relief for India (India). 15 reports from WION, The Hindu, INDIA New England News and 10 more. Related: “Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal says proposed India-US trade deal will protect farmers’ interests”. Ongoing: also reported on 3 of the previous 7 days (first 25 Oct).

Capital goods & infra: mild tailwind (+1) — Engineering exports gain access

Why it matters: Lower tariffs or a trade deal open markets for Indian exporters and attract investment into export manufacturing.

Market gauges: Growth outlook +1, Rupee +1, Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +1

Confidence: high · horizon: months

item.title: [+1] India To Remain Worlds Fastest-Growing Major Economy Through 2027 With 7% GDP Growth, Report Highlights IMF
item.description:
Signal: stronger Indian growth data (India). 9 reports from Moneycontrol.com, News On AIR, www.biltraxmedia.com and 5 more. Related: “India's diesel exports hit 13-month high amid Iran war: How refiners are cashing in on supply disruptions”. New in the last 24 hours.

Capital goods & infra: mild tailwind (+1) — Orders and capex firm

Why it matters: Better activity data points to firmer demand, orders and credit growth, supporting earnings across cyclical sectors.

Market gauges: Growth outlook +3, Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks

item.title: [+1] Silver Is Falling Despite Lower Treasury Yields and a Persistent Supply Deficit
item.description:
Signal: lower metal prices. 3 reports from Investing.com, BigGo Finance, Shanghai Metals Market. Related: “Silver Slips Below $51 an Ounce as Hot Inflation Lifts December Fed Rate-Hike Odds to 75%”. Mixed: 2 reports point the other way. New in the last 24 hours.

Capital goods & infra: mild tailwind (+1) — Input costs ease

Why it matters: Falling metal prices cut Indian producers' realisations, often on weak Chinese demand, while easing input costs for manufacturers.

Confidence: low · horizon: weeks
